passages.note: Bill history lists Bolick as a co-sponsor of SB1165, a single-subject biological-sex athletics bill.

passages.provision_quote: B. Athletic teams or sports designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex. C. This section does not restrict the eligibility of any student to participate in any interscholastic or intramural athletic team or sport designated as being for "males", "men" or "boys" or designated as "coed" or "mixed".
passages.note: Enacted text requires sex-based team designation while leaving transgender students free to compete on male or coed teams, excluding a total ban.
House Third Reading roll call shows Bolick voting Y to pass SB1165.

rows.reasoning: Bolick co-sponsored SB 1165 (2022) and voted Y on its House Third Reading (Passed 31-24-5-0-0); the enacted law requires that teams designated for "females", "women" or "girls" not be open to students of the male sex, while expressly leaving transgender students free to compete on male or coed teams. This matches the rung's text requiring transgender athletes to "compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth" and excludes the complete ban described in rung 5.
